reviews.decision_reason: select_demand admits every supplied corpus row because the threshold is demand_score >= 3 and all eight records meet it. That contradicts the assigned job output, which contains only n06-r01, and introduces lower-priority or weakly supported demand candidates before normalization hides them.

normalize masks the over-selection by forcing index_window = [0] and returning only head(1). That produces the observed single-record needs artifact, but the boundary role says it should normalize selected evidence while preserving allowed identifiers and a bounded index window, not silently discard seven selected records. This makes missing or contradictory demand evidence invisible downstream.

assemble_provenance receives the already-truncated normalized needs table and deterministically emits ranked provenance using record_id, source_id, source_weight, and rank. No local fault is visible in this boundary; its incomplete output is inherited from normalize.
